notes_pl: Prompty do przemalowania broni i portretu tak, by były malarstwem, a nie cyfrową ilustracją. Nic jeszcze nie wygenerowano.

Powód: atlasy v09 powstały z promptów, które prosiły o 'polished worn steel edges' i 'physical brass cartridges'. Stąd chrom, mosiądz i plastikowe łuski. Shader painterly.lua tylko to tłumi i nie przerysuje kształtów.
Zalecany tryb: edycja obrazu z bieżącym atlasem jako referencją póz (referenced_image_paths), by zachować timing animacji i rejestrację nadgarstków.
Styl wspólny jest w polu shared_style; należy go wkleić na początek każdego promptu, jeśli narzędzie nie łączy pól.
Szczegóły podłączenia nowego atlasu są w polu integration przy każdym zasobie.
shared_style: Painted as a late-medieval / early-Renaissance religious panel and fresco, then reduced to crisp, deliberately clustered 16-bit pixel art with a limited palette. Egg tempera and thin oil glazes over a dark toned ground. Matte surfaces everywhere: form is modelled by value and chiaroscuro (light falling from one side, deep umber shadow on the other), never by specular reflections. Historical pigments only: bone black, burnt umber, raw umber, yellow ochre, aged warm lead white for the lights, madder lake and dulled vermilion ONLY for blood and cloth, very sparing verdigris. Gold appears only as worn gold leaf with red bole showing through rubbed edges. Every form is bounded by a dark painted contour line (sinopia / ink outline) as in fresco. References and what to take from each: Giovanni da Modena, Inferno, Bolognini Chapel, San Petronio, Bologna: scorched fresco palette, coarse confident outlines, bodily, repellent horror. Hieronymus Bosch, right (hell) wing of The Garden of Earthly Delights: everyday objects turned into instruments of torment, grotesque hybrid ornament, small tormented figures as carved decoration. Hans Memling, The Last Judgment (Gdansk): pale bodies against a dark ground, ordered composition, gilded framing, gestures of dread. Michelangelo, The Last Judgment, Sistine Chapel: heavy anatomy, tense twisting hands, forearms and knuckles carrying real weight.
shared_negative: No chrome, no mirror or specular highlights, no glossy or wet-looking metal, no plastic, no red plastic shotgun shells, no polished or shiny brass, no airbrushed gradients, no 3D render look, no modern digital concept-art or 'grimdark game art' rendering, no anime or manga linework, no bloom, glow, lens flare or neon, no comic-book starburst muzzle flash, no text, numbers, labels, grid lines, frame borders or watermark.

assets.prompt: [shared_style] Edit this existing 16-frame first-person double-barrelled shotgun animation sheet. Keep EXACTLY all sixteen poses, the camera angle, hand positions, barrel directions, cell order and transparent background. Repaint only the material and ornament. The gun is a heavy hand-forged funerary object: blackened, pitted iron barrels painted as matte dark umber-grey with ochre-lit edges; a stock of dark walnut; the action plate carries a carved bone relief of a screaming, tormented face and small bodies in the manner of Bosch's hell, flanked by curved bone horns; worn gold-leaf fillets with red bole showing. The hands wear old black-brown leather gauntlets with iron plates, modelled like Michelangelo's heavy, tense hands. Cartridges are period paper-hulled shells: waxed brown paper, dark tarnished almost black brass heads, no shine. Frame 1 idle aimed; frame 2 fires: the flash is a short painted tongue of flame like the fires in Bosch's hell, ochre and dull vermilion with soot, flat and compact, not a starburst; frames 3-4 recoil with thin grey-brown painted smoke; frame 5 back to idle; frames 6-8 the breech breaks open and tilts, the two open chambers seen from the rear as dark iron rings; frames 9-12 the left hand brings two paper shells, inserts them, withdraws; frames 13-15 the action closes and returns to aim; frame 16 identical to frame 1. [shared_negative]

assets.layout: 1536 x 1024 px, EXACTLY 6 portraits in a 3 x 2 grid of equal square cells (512 x 512), order: top row 1-2-3, bottom row 4-5-6. Opaque dark umber toned ground in every cell (not transparent). The same man, same scale and head position in every cell. Framing for the HUD arch mask: head-and-shoulders bust centred horizontally; the top of the hair no higher than 20 percent of the cell height; eyes at about 42 percent; chin at about 68 percent; shoulders and armour reach the bottom edge. assets.prompt: [shared_style] A series of six head-and-shoulders portraits of the same man, painted as a small devotional panel portrait in the manner of Hans Memling: a pale, lit face against a near-black umber ground, one-sided light, precise painted contours, lead-white highlights on the brow, cheekbone and nose, warm umber shadows. He is an ordinary human with no magic who walks through hell: a harsh, weathered face, short untidy black hair, a scar across the brow and cheek, wearing heavy dark battered plate armour over a dark gambeson. The posture and presence recall Guts from Berserk, but this is an old-master painting, not a manga or anime drawing: no manga eyes, no cel shading, no ink-pen hair. The weight and tension of the neck and jaw come from Michelangelo's Last Judgment; the bruised, bloodied flesh in the later frames comes from Giovanni da Modena's Inferno, restrained, never gory. Expression: exhaustion, vigilance, determination and restrained anger, never a triumphant hero's pose. 1: frontal, guarded, a hard stare. 2: head turned toward the viewer's left, glancing aside. 3: head turned toward the viewer's right. 4: struck: eyes squeezed shut, jaw clenched, a fresh cut. 5: critical: exhausted, eyes lowered, blood running from the brow and mouth, the skin greyer. 6: firing: teeth bared in a grimace against the recoil, head slightly turned. [shared_negative]

assets.lettering_style: Lettering painted directly on a fresco wall in the manner of the inscriptions and captions in Giovanni da Modena's Inferno (Bolognini Chapel, San Petronio, Bologna) and of the Gothic majuscule captions in late-medieval Italian fresco cycles: Gothic majuscule / Lombardic capitals, broad confident brush strokes, stroke ends finished with small split serifs, hairline flourishes kept minimal. Each letter is painted in warm lime white (aged, slightly yellowed, not pure white) with a thin dark sinopia-brown contour line all around, and a narrow red-ochre inner stroke or small red-ochre dot ornament on the thick stems only, like rubrication. Matte, flat, tempera-on-plaster look: subtle uneven brush density inside the strokes, no gradients, no bevels, no metallic or gold leaf, no drop shadows, no 3D, no glow. Readability is the first requirement: each letter must remain unmistakable when reduced to 11-18 px tall, so the silhouettes are bold and simple, counters are open, ornament never closes a counter or crosses a neighbouring letter, and the Polish diacritics (ogonek, kreska, kropka, Ł stroke) are large, separate and clearly attached to their letter. Background: completely transparent alpha, no plaster texture behind the letters, no frame, no grid lines, no labels, no numbering.
